American Countess Review

Review of American Countess

The 2020-built (2021-inaugurated, scrapped in 2024) cruise ship American Countess was a newbuild paddlewheel steamboat reconstructed using the hull of MS Kanesville Queen (1995-built paddle-wheeler and casino ship of "Harrah’s Council Bluffs Casino and Hotel").

The vessel (MMSI 368048990) was originally scheduled to enter service on April 5, 2020 (inaugural cruise), following a drydock lengthening project by Gulf Island Fabrication Inc at Gulf Island Shipyard in Houma, Louisiana.

The 246-passenger riverboat was the fourth and final vessel in the USA-flagged fleet of American Queen Voyages (formerly AQSC), alongside American Duchess (2017), American Empress (2003), and American Queen (1995).

The lengthening involved cutting the existing hull in two and inserting a 60 ft (18 m) prefabricated midship section. Nearly 150 workers were involved in the reconstruction project.

The vessel’s previous owner was Hornblower Group Inc (via Hornblower Cruises and Events).

After Hornblower Group declared bankruptcy in February 2024, American Queen Voyages was placed for sale. Hornblower was sold to Strategic Value Partners, which announced reorganization plans to focus on its other subsidiaries.

In a Texas-based auction in March 2024, ACL/American Cruise Lines emerged as the highest bidder and acquired four riverboats—American Countess (US$1.6M), American Duchess (US$0.2M), American Empress (US$1.6M), and American Queen (US$2.15M)—along with other AQV assets.

In May 2024, ACL announced that American Countess, American Duchess, and American Queen would be scrapped. American Countess’ AIS last transmitted on May 2 at 13:49 UTC, showing the vessel at MARS (Modern American Recycling Service Inc's yard) in Houma, Louisiana.

Decks and Cabins

American Countess staterooms (123 total) were primarily balcony cabins, excluding 43 Interior cabins. Each veranda featured two wicker chairs and a cocktail table.

Cabin amenities included individually controlled air-conditioning, smart HDTV (with satellite reception), dark wood wardrobe, dressers (ample drawer space), mini-bar (fridge), electronic safe (in closet), direct-dial phone, alarm clock, Keurig brewer (tea/coffee), binoculars (in-cabin use), Clarins toiletries, terry robes, hairdryer, and abundant outlets and lighting.

Staterooms, like the ship’s public rooms, were styled with Victorian-era decor, featuring polished wood, period wallpaper patterns, framed paintings, and comfortable beds with luxury bedding and under-bed storage.

Handicap/wheelchair-accessible cabins were available. There were no connecting or family cabins.

The vessel had 8 decks, with accommodations on 2 decks. Three elevators (1 aft, 2 forward) serviced decks 1 through 3.

Shipboard Facilities and Amenities

The American Countess featured classic decor similar to American Queen and American Empress. Complimentary shore excursions were offered at all ports, conducted via the company’s modern motorcoaches providing hop-on-hop-off tours.

Complimentary beverages (local wines and beers) were served with dinner in the main dining room, which also offered open seating for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. The ship featured a specialty dining venue separate from the main restaurant.

  • The Fitness Center was equipped with modern cardio machines (treadmills, bikes), a workout bench, dumbbells, and free weights, all with scenic river views.
  • Perks SPA
  • The Theater hosted nightly Broadway-style shows and lectures from guest historians focused on American heritage and culture.
  • Grand Lobby
  • The Grand Dining Room, staffed by an award-winning culinary team, featured refined decor with walnut accents and Italian fabrics. Large windows provided scenic river views.
  • The Library
  • The Card Room offered a social setting for games and mingling.
  • The River Grill offered a more casual atmosphere with its own bar and outdoor terrace seating. It accommodated half the guests of the main dining room.
  • Chart Room

The Sun Deck included a Walking Track, shaded seating, and the Pilot House (Navigation Bridge).

Inaugural Itineraries 2020

American Countess cruised on the Ohio and Lower Mississippi Rivers (including tributaries), with various itineraries from Memphis, Tennessee and New Orleans, Louisiana, typically lasting 7 days and themed on the Antebellum South and the American Civil War.

Below are the planned 2020 itineraries, which were eventually canceled due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Homeport departures were at 5 PM; arrivals at 8 AM.

  • 7-night New Orleans to Memphis
  • 7-night Memphis to Alton
  • 7-night Alton to Louisville
  • 7-night Louisville to Pittsburgh
  • 7-night Pittsburgh to Louisville
  • 7-night Louisville to Memphis
  • 7-night Alton to Red Wing
  • 7-night Red Wing to Alton
  • 14-night Red Wing to New Orleans
  • 7-night Memphis to Chattanooga
  • 7-night Chattanooga to Memphis
  • 7-night roundtrip New Orleans
  • 5-night roundtrip New Orleans

The Maiden Voyage (March 21–28, 2021) was a 7-day roundtrip from New Orleans, visiting Nottoway Plantation and Natchez.

American Queen Steamboat Company Cruise Deals

American Countess cruise packages were all-inclusive and covered:

  • All shore excursions ("Steamcoach Tours")
  • 1-night pre-cruise hotel stay
  • Soft drinks and bottled water throughout the cruise
  • Wines and beers with dinner
  • 24-hour room service (breakfast fare, sandwiches, burgers, salmon, macaroni & cheese, desserts)
  • Wi-Fi Internet
  • Pilot House tour
  • Smoking was prohibited inside cabins and on balconies; allowed only on the Sun Deck.

"Commodore Services" offered exclusive perks for guests in LFS-Loft and OS-Owner Suites, including:

  • Welcome gifts (fruit basket, wine bottle)
  • Suite tour
  • Priority boarding and dining
  • Reserved balcony seating in the Theater with personal escort
  • Private reception with the Captain and Senior Officers
  • Personal River Butler
  • Unpacking/packing assistance, laundry, pressing, shoeshine
  • In-cabin dining services (Afternoon Tea, meals on the balcony, canapés, desserts)

American Countess Wiki

The casino ship MS Kanesville Queen was acquired by AQSC in 2016. The vessel had IMO number 8642921, a length overall (LOA) of 83 m (272 ft), a hull length of 80 m (264 ft), a beam of 24 m (78 ft), and a gross tonnage of 6837 tons. The Main Deck Casino covered an area of 1177 m² (12,670 ft²), while the Upper Deck Casino spanned 1269 m² (13,660 ft²).

After the acquisition, the vessel was relocated from Council Bluffs to Jeffersonville, Indiana, where it was docked at the Marine Builders Inc shipyard. In October 2018, under her own power, the ship departed Jeffersonville and arrived in Houma, Louisiana, where reconstruction began.

The ship's lengthening project included the addition of a 60-ft (18.3-m) midship prefabricated section, encompassing both hull and superstructure.

The American Countess riverboat successfully completed river trials on February 19, 2020. The trials were conducted on the waterway section between Houma and Morgan City, Louisiana. The christening ceremony was initially planned for April 4, 2020, in New Orleans, to be followed by the Maiden Voyage on April 5.

On March 21, 2021, the christening ceremony was held in New Orleans, led by godmother Angie Hack, daughter of John Waggoner, AQSC’s CEO and founder. The ceremony was attended by John Waggoner, Billy Nungesser (Louisiana’s Lieutenant Governor), Brandy Christian (President and CEO of Port NOLA), and Kevin Rabbitt (CEO of Hornblower Group).

The American Countess' Inaugural Cruise was a 7-day "VIP Cruise" along the Mississippi River, from March 21-28, 2021. The roundtrip itinerary from New Orleans included visits to Nottoway Plantation and Natchez.

In August 2022, AQV announced the introduction of a new 23-day itinerary, "Grand Ohio and Upper Mississippi Rivers," scheduled for summer 2023 aboard American Countess. The northbound voyage (Minneapolis to Pittsburgh) was set to depart on July 24, with the reverse route (Pittsburgh to Minneapolis) departing on August 14. The itinerary covered 1772 mi (2850 km) of river cruising, visiting 19 port cities across 10 states: MN (Red Wing), WI (La Crosse), IA (Dubuque, Bettendorf, Burlington), MO (Hannibal, St. Louis, Kimmswick, Cape Girardeau), KY (Paducah, Henderson, Owensboro, Brandenburg, Louisville), IN (Madison), OH (Cincinnati), KY (Maysville), WV (Point Pleasant), GA (Marietta).
